summary: A grid of pieces of a few colours, not always a rectangle. A move swaps two neighbouring pieces so that three or more of one colour line up; those are removed, pieces above fall, new ones come in, and lines that form so are removed too. A swap that lines nothing up is undone. An obstacle is never swapped and lines up with nothing. A piece held in place (chained, frozen) is not swapped but lines up by its colour, which frees it. Four or more in a line, or four in a square, leave a piece with a power. A layer under the pieces (jelly, grass) is taken off by clearing or spread by lines on it.

cells.looks: one piece; its colour is what it is, whatever its shape or face
a cell of the grid filled by something that is not one of the pieces being swapped: an obstacle, a block, a covered or locked cell
a place inside the grid's bounding rectangle where the grid has no cell (outside an outline that is not a rectangle, a gap)
a cell hidden by an animation, a dialog or a piece in mid-fall

state_fields.grid: rows of the grid's bounding rectangle from the top, each a list of cells from the left: a piece is its colour's number (1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue, 6 purple, 7 pink, 8 white, 9 cyan, 10 brown; always the same for one kind of piece); a piece with a power (striped, a rocket, a bomb) is 500 plus its colour's number, or 500 with no colour; a piece held in place that still shows its colour (chained, frozen) is 20 plus its colour's number; 11 something fixed that shows no piece (a box, a locked cell), 12 such a thing that falls; 0 no cell or nothing in it; null a cell nobody read
state_fields.score: the game's score as read, or null
state_fields.scene: the id of the scene the screen shows
state_fields.under: only when some cell has a layer under its piece (jelly, grass, carpet, a tinted tile), drawn beneath the piece and seen around it: the rows of the same rectangle, each cell the number of such layers (0 none); leave the field out when no cell has one. Something over a cell that hides or holds what is in it (a bubble, a box, a cage around a thing that is no piece) is no layer: that cell is 11

actions.description: drag the piece at `cell` onto its neighbour at `to` ([row, column] each)
tap the piece with a power at `cell` to set it off, in a game that takes that

scenes.looks: the grid at rest, waiting for a swap
the game's own message that the level or game is won
the game's own message that it is over (no moves or time left)

meta_actions.description: start another game or level after the end

colours.description: how many colours the game's own pieces come in (only the simulated game draws by it)

square.description: whether four of one colour in a two-by-two square is a move; null until the game showed it

swap_power.description: whether a piece with a power goes off when swapped with any neighbour; null until the game showed it

tap_power.description: whether a piece with a power goes off when tapped; null until the game showed it

pair_power.description: whether two pieces with a power swapped with each other go off (and one that clears a colour swapped with anything); null until the game showed it

goals.description: the level's goals as the screen showed them: each its kind (collect, cover, bring_down, other), the value of the cells it is about (null when nothing on the board looks like its picture) and how many are still to go; null until a screen showed them

beside.description: whether something fixed that is no piece (an obstacle, a box) is broken, a layer at a time, by a line cleared beside it; null until the game showed it

spread.description: whether the layer under the pieces is one a line spreads (a line with a cell on it lays it under its other cells) and not one clearing takes off; null until a goal or the game showed it

panel.moves: the tight box [left, top, width, height] in whole-screen image pixels around the number of moves (or the time) left in this level, the digits alone
panel.goals: a list with one entry per goal of the level the screen shows (beside or above the board): {"box": the tight box [left, top, width, height] in whole-screen image pixels around the goal's picture alone, "count": the number shown with it, how many are still to go (0 when it shows a tick), "kind": "collect" (clear or collect that many), "cover" (lay the layer pictured, such as grass or carpet, under that many more cells by making lines on it), "bring_down" (bring what is pictured to the bottom) or "other" (a score, or anything else), "about": what on the board the goal is about: "pieces" (the board's pieces of the colour pictured), "layer" (a layer under the pieces: jelly, grass, carpet), "fixed" (things fixed in cells that a line beside or on them breaks: boxes, bubbles, stones, and anything held inside them), "held" (pieces held in place: chained, frozen), "falls" (things that fall and are no piece), or "other"}
